safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Increase SAP safety lead time from 0.0 to 1.8 days

narrative: Demand for PL3__MA7F4613 is erratic (CV=0.593) with a right-skewed distribution and a high non-zero fraction (94.7%), indicating a high-runner item with significant day-to-day variability. Lead times are volatile (CV=0.786, mean=1.14 days), making lead-time uncertainty the dominant risk driver (66.7% of total variance). A continuous-review (r,Q) policy was selected: the large EOQ-derived order quantity amortises ordering costs efficiently, while the elevated safety stock of 2,793 units (vs. SAP 777) provides the required 95% service coverage. The storage cap of 10,907 units binds and reduces the order quantity from 9,526 to 8,114 units.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint binds: EOQ 9526 capped to 8114 units. SS+OQ=10907 <= 10907.748 — feasible.

research_insights.selection_rationale: High-frequency, largely non-zero erratic demand with volatile lead times suits a continuous-review fixed-order-quantity model. The EOQ minimises total ordering and holding costs, and the reorder point absorbs combined demand and lead-time uncertainty at the 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap reduces order quantity by 1,412 units (14.8% below EOQ). This slightly increases ordering frequency and annual ordering cost but remains well within feasibility. Service level is unaffected as safety stock is unchanged.
